{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2025}}

'''Ted Joseph Case''' (19 July 1947 – 31 December 2015) was an American biologist and ecologist affiliated with the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name="Memoriam" /> He joined the faculty of UC San Diego in 1978, and was later elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2004.<ref name="AAAS">{{Cite web |date=9 February 2023 |title=Ted J. Case |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/ted-j-case |access-date=27 March 2025 |website=Member Directory |publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] |language=en}}</ref> Case was known for his contributions to ecology, including multiple books on [[community ecology|community]] and [[theoretical ecology]].

Born on 19 July 1947 in [[Sioux City, Iowa]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 April 2016 |title=Case, Ted J. |url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n82112939.html |access-date=26 March 2025 |website=LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies |publisher=[[Library of Congress]]}}</ref> Case attended the [[University of Redlands]] and graduated with a bachelor's degree in 1969. He received a Ph.D. from the [[University of California, Irvine]] in 1974 and pursued postdoctoral research at the [[University of California, Davis]]. In 1975, Case joined [[Purdue University]] as a faculty member, but in 1978 he moved to the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name="Memoriam">{{Cite web |date=5 April 2016 |title=In Memoriam, Ted J. Case, 1947-2015 |url=https://biology.ucsd.edu/about/news/article_040516.html |access-date=26 March 2025 |website=School of Biological Sciences |publisher=[[UC San Diego]]}}{{Unbulleted list|{{Cite web |last=Nieh |first=James |title=In Memoriam: Case, Ted J. |url=http://senate.universityofcalifornia.edu/_files/inmemoriam/html/TedJ.Case.html |website=Academic Senate |publisher=[[University of California]] |access-date=26 March 2025}}}}</ref>

The [[University of California Press]] published Ted J. Case and [[Martin L. Cody]]'s book ''Island Biogeography in the Sea of Cortéz'' in 1983.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Island Biogeography in the Sea of Cortéz |date=1983 |publisher=[[University of California Press]] |isbn=978-0-520-04799-0 |editor-last=Case |editor-first=Ted J. |editor-last2=Cody |editor-first2=Martin L. |editor-link2=Martin L. Cody}}</ref> Case went on to coedit with [[Jared Diamond]] the book ''Community Ecology'', which was published by [[Harper & Row]] in 1986 as a broad overview of the field including chapters contributed by 35 authors.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Community Ecology |date=1986 |publisher=[[Harper & Row]] |isbn=978-0-06-041202-9 |editor-last=Diamond |editor-first=Jared |editor-link=Jared Diamond |editor-last2=Case |editor-first2=Ted J.}}</ref> In 1999, [[Oxford University Press]] published Case's ''An Illustrated Guide to Theoretical Ecology'', which includes analysis of the mathematical formulas underpinning theoretical ecology, supplemented with graphs and other visualizations.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Case |first=Ted J. |url=https://global.oup.com/ushe/product/an-illustrated-guide-to-theoretical-ecology-9780195085129?cc=us&lang=en |title=An Illustrated Guide to Theoretical Ecology |date=1999 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=978-0-19-508512-9}}</ref> In 2004, Case was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="AAAS" /> He "died of a sudden heart attack while trail running on December 31, 2015", aged 68 years old.<ref name="Memoriam" />
